newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares close higher on local funds support.
newsitem.headline: KL shares close higher on local funds support.

text.p: Malaysian shares rebounded to close higher on Friday as local funds stepped in to buy in the afternoon session, dealers and fund managers said.
At the close, the key Composite Index of leading shares was up 9.09 points or 0.90 percent to 1,017.61. The second board index rose 17.74 points or 3.34 percent to 548.46.
The rise in the key index follows nearly 10-days of selling down triggered by foreigners exiting on fears of regional economic instability and better returns elsewhere.
"I believe there was support by government intervention," said a dealing manager at a large local brokerage.
Among the stocks that funds bought were RHB Capital, Maybank, and Sime Darby.
"The banks and Sime Darby have been the target of the short selling (in the morning) because of their liquidity," said Ramlan Ahmad, senior manager at fund managers Commerce MGI.
The Composite Index had dipped to a new one-and-a-half year low of 988.47 in morning trade.
The de facto devaluation of the Philippine peso earlier on Friday had induced speculators to attack the ringgit.
"The scare was that Malaysia would also be targetted by the hedge funds," said Ramlan.
The Philippines Central Bank said on Friday it would allow the peso to trade in a wider range against the U.S. dollar, with immediate effect.

"We're rebounding on Tun Daim's statement and a lot of local fund support," said Ang Kok Heng, general manager at TA Asset Management, referring to market-supportive comments on Thursday by Economic Advisor to the Government, Daim Zainuddin.
"The market is still very volatile as there's selling by foreign funds on stocks as well as ringgit. The two combined together make it very complicated," added Ang.
Other index heavyweights that rebounded sharply included Tenaga, falling to 10.90 ringgit, before rebounding to 11.30 ringgit, but still 30 cents shy of its close on Thursday.
Telekom fell to a low of 10.70 ringgit, but ended 10 cents higher at 11.00 ringgit.

"The market went almost down to 980, but it did not touch it. The risks are very low at these levels, because the downside is very limited. It's time to buy," said Tony Shue, institutional dealer at Jupiter Securities.
"I think the speculators will lose money this round," he added.

Ballooning interbank rates on Friday were the effect of central Bank Negara's massive intervention in the foreign exchange market earlier this week. But continued jumps in interest rates would induce speculators to once again look to stocks for their shorting activities, said analysts.
"If they keep driving interest rates up, the stock sellers will be back," said Simon Maughan, head of research at brokers W.I. Carr in Kuala Lumpur.
Overnight interbank rates ended at 10/15 percent on Friday after peaking at 45 percent.
Volume totalled 325 million shares valued at 2.27 billion ringgit. Gainers outpaced losers 571 to 132.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange the spot July contract gained 15.1 points to 1,017.7 with 2,325 lots traded. August futures gained 8.0 points to 1,015.7 with 27 lots traded. September gained 1.2 points to 1,018.8 with three lots changing hands.
-- Azhar Sukri (603-206 2323)
